# LinkedIn Company Search Scraper (No Cookies)

The Apify actor [`harvestapi/linkedin-company-search`](https://apify.com/harvestapi/linkedin-company-search) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.21**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Search for LinkedIn companies with filters and extract detailed company information. No cookies or account required. Fast and reliable actor

## Pricing

Pay per event — Actor Start $0.001, Short company $0.002, Full company $0.004 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/harvestapi/linkedin-company-search) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/harvestapi-linkedin-company-search@0.0.21#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scraperMode` | string |  |  | Company Scraper Mode — Choose the mode for scraping LinkedIn companies. The Short mode provides basic information, while the Full mode includes full detailed company data. |
| `maxItems` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of companies to scrape — Maximum number of companies to scrape. The actor will stop scraping when this limit is reached. |
| `searchQuery` | string |  |  | Search query — Query to search LinkedIn companies. (e.g., `marketing`). [The query supports search operators](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a524335) |
| `locations` | array |  |  | Locations Filter — Filter Companies by these LinkedIn locations. Example: `San Francisco`. LinkedIn does not always understand your text queries. For example for "UK" query it will apply "Ukraine" location, so you should use "United Kingdom" in this case. Try this out first in the location filter in |
| `industryIds` | array |  |  | Industry IDs Filter — Filter Companies by these LinkedIn industry IDs. Example: `4` for 'Software Development'. Full list: `https://github.com/HarvestAPI/linkedin-industry-codes-v2/blob/main/linkedin_industry_code_v2_all_eng_with_header.csv` |
| `companySize` | string[] |  |  | Company Size Filter (filters by the company size specified in the company "About" tab) — Filter Companies by these company size ranges. |
| `startPage` | integer |  | `1` | Start Page — The page number to start scraping from. The last page is 20, according to LinkedIn limitations. |
| `takePages` | integer |  |  | Scrape search pages — The number of search pages to scrape. Each page contains 50 companies. The last page is 20, according to LinkedIn limitations. |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
